newsitem.title: USA: Millennium says identifies diabetes gene.
newsitem.headline: Millennium says identifies diabetes gene.

text.p: Millennium Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Thursday that it had identified a gene implicated in the development of type II diabetes.
The finding triggered a milestone payment to Millennium from its partner, Hoffman-LaRoche Inc, U.S. affliate of Swiss pharmaceutical group Roche Holding Ltd.

Frank Lee, chief scientific officer at Millennium, said the company's scientists used positional cloning techniques to detect the presence of a mutation of the gene, leading them to associat the gene with the development of type II diabetes.
Millennium said that neither it nor Roche would provide more specific scientific details on the research until a scientific manuscript had been published in a peer-reviewed journal.
Identification of a gene can lead to a greater understanding of how a disease works and eventually lead to drugs for treating the disease or its cure.
Type II, or non-insulin dependent diabetes, accounts for about 90 percent of diabetics and is a metabolic disorder resulting from the body's inability to make enough, or properly use, insulin.
In May, researchers from the Howard Hughes Medical Institute at the Universty of Chicago said they had identified markers for the first gene linked to type II diabetes.

They studied a group of Mexican Americans and narrowed their search area to one end of chromosome 2. That particular gene is believed to be linked to diabetes in Mexican American and thought to play a smaller role in diabetes in other ethnic groups.
